paper.title_en: Local patch analysis of ACT DR6 convergence map using morphological statistics
paper.abstract_en: We perform a hierarchical, multi-scale morphological analysis to search for anomalous behavior in the large-scale matter distribution using the Atacama Cosmology Telescope Data Release 6 (ACT DR6) convergence map. Employing Minkowski functionals, contour Minkowski tensors, and Betti numbers, we measure their deviations from ensemble expectations and median values obtained from isotropic $Λ$CDM simulations provided by ACT. To assess statistical significance, we develop a general methodology based on the persistence of anomalies across threshold ranges and spatial resolutions, accounting for correlations among the statistics. Analyzing both the full dataset and hemispherical subregions reveals overall consistency with isotropic $Λ$CDM expectations. Because localized deviations may be diluted over larger areas, we further examine individual sky patches, identifying several regions with statistically significant deviations that we designate as anomalous. In particular, positive density fluctuations near the CMB Cold Spot are anomalous, exceeding the 99% confidence level, and overlap with a previously reported anomalous southern spot in Planck CMB temperature data. Analysis of the corresponding null map indicates potential contamination from residual foregrounds or instrumental systematics. Comparing the anomalous patches in ACT with those from a previous Planck convergence map analysis reveals no overlapping regions, suggesting that the Planck anomalies are likely attributable to noise. Further investigation of these atypical patches, considering residual foregrounds, instrumental systematics, reconstruction noise, and independent large-scale structure surveys, is warranted to determine their physical origin.
